source.snippet: I have a @RestResource endpoint that is available for guest users on a Digital Experience Site. Should I worry about users making lots of requests and implement rate limiting? Are there any mechanisms in Salesforce/Apex that are already preventing this from happening? If not, are there any known patterns for how to go about implementing such a mechanism in Salesforce?

problem_statement: Salesforce developers exposing public REST endpoints on Experience Cloud sites lack built-in rate limiting primitives in Apex, forcing them to hand-roll abuse-prevention logic or leave guest-facing APIs unprotected — a security and cost risk on a paid enterprise platform.
target_segment: Salesforce developers and architects at companies running public-facing Digital Experience Sites with guest user API access
notes: Single signal but enterprise context is strong — Salesforce orgs are expensive and abuse of guest APIs can blow through governor limits with real cost consequences. A managed AppExchange component or documented pattern service could sell. Needs more signals to validate breadth of pain.
